name: @kepler.gl/mcp

tools.name: map_set-basemap
tools.description: Change the basemap style of the kepler.gl map.

tools.name: map_set-view-mode
tools.description:
Switch the map between the flat 2D map, the tilted 3D map and the 3D globe.
- '2d': flat map, no tilt.
- '3d': flat map tilted (pitch 50), for extruded/3D layers.
- 'globe': the 3D globe — use it when the data spans the world and the user is looking at global patterns.
Globe support: point, arc, line, trip, cluster, hexagon, grid, geojson and vector-tile layers render on the globe. The 'flow' and 'flowField' layers are NOT supported there yet (flow arrows collapse edge-on; flow field clipping is mercator-only), so keep those on the 2d/3d map.

tools.name: map_get-boundary
tools.description: Get the boundary of the map. Northwest and Southeast coordinates in [longitude, latitude] format.

tools.name: map_add-layer
tools.description:
Add a kepler.gl map layer from a dataset.
IMPORTANT: generated layer names must be unique.

LAYER TYPES:
- point: Point markers (requires lat/lng columns)
- flow: Origin->destination flow map (requires two point lat/lng pairs, auto-detected)
- flowField: Animated streamlines over a vector field (u/v, speed/direction, or altitude)
- h3: H3 hexagon cells (requires hexId column)
- geojson: Polygon/geometry features (uses geometry column, usually auto-detected)
- hexagon: Hexagonal binning of points
- heatmap: Heat map visualization
- cluster: Clustered point visualization
- arc/line: Arc or line connections between points
- grid: Grid binning
- trip: Animated trip (flights, deliveries, vessels)
- s2: S2 geometry cells
- a5/geohash: Indexed cells (columns.token)
- icon: Markers with named icons (columns.lat/lng/icon)
- 3D: glTF models at points or geometry centroids (columns, options.scenegraph)
- bitmap/vectorTile/rasterTile/wms/tile3d: Matching datasets imported with map.load-tileset
- contour: Density contours or a scalar surface (lat/lng or geometry; optional contour.weightColumn)
- voronoi: Nearest-site mosaic (lat/lng or geometry centroids; voronoi.boundsPadding)
- zarr: Raster variable from a Zarr dataset imported with map.load-zarr (zarr.variable, dimensionIndexes, axis, frame, rescale)

FLOW MAPS (layerType 'flow'):
For origin->destination flows use layerType 'flow' — a dedicated flow layer that draws
locations and weighted flows between them. It needs TWO point lat/lng pairs in the
dataset (source pair + destination pair), which are auto-detected. Prefer 'flow' over
'arc' for O-D flows; 'arc' draws straight great-circle lines without location clustering
or flow aggregation. To weight the flows by a value column (flow magnitude), pass
countColumn with the column name — omit it to render all flows at weight 1.

FLOW FIELD (layerType 'flowField'):
Animated streamlines over a vector field — wind, currents, or downhill flow. It is NOT
the origin->destination 'flow' layer: 'flow' joins two point pairs, 'flowField' draws
many short lines through a field of vectors, one row per sample point.
The direction comes from one of three column sets, auto-detected in this order:
- u/v components (default mode 'UV'), optionally with an altitude column
- speed + direction (mode 'SPEED_DIR')
- altitude only (mode 'ELEVATION'): the downhill gradient gives the direction
Position is lat/lng (auto-detected, or latitudeColumn/longitudeColumn) or a GeoJSON
geometry column. When the dataset names the columns differently, pass flowField.mode
plus flowField.uColumn/vColumn/speedColumn/directionColumn/altitudeColumn.
Set flowField.colorBySpeed true to color lines by local speed; otherwise simpleColor
applies. colorBy/colorMap do not apply to this layer. Do NOT add a time filter — the
flow field animates itself.

BASIC MAP:
- Use datasetName, latitudeColumn/longitudeColumn (for point maps), and layerType
- Omit color-related parameters for simple visualization, use simpleColor instead.

COLOR MAPPING:
- If user requests color visualization, use available columns in the dataset
- Use geoda.analysis (analysis: 'classify') to classify data into bins or unique values when needed
- For continuous data (colorType 'breaks'):
  [{value: 0, color: '#fee5d9'}, {value: 50, color: '#fcae91'}, {value: 100, color: '#fb6a4a'}, {value: null, color: '#de2d26'}]
  The last entry with value: null represents the color for the highest values
- For categorical data (colorType 'unique'):
  [{value: 'category1', color: '#1f77b4'}, {value: 'category2', color: '#ff7f0e'}]
  HARD RULE: the colorMap values MUST be the actual unique values present in the data.
  Call geoda.analysis (analysis: 'classify', method: 'unique values') first and use the
  returned uniqueValues verbatim. NEVER invent category labels from the field name —
  the command rejects values that do not exist in the data.
- If the user doesn't specify colors, omit colorBy/colorMap — kepler.gl applies its default color range automatically

For geojson datasets:
- Use geometryColumn: '_geojson' and layerType: 'geojson' even for point collections

datasetName.description: The name (label) or id of the dataset. Prefer the label when known.

geometryColumn.description: Geometry field for contour or voronoi.

columns.description: Explicit mappings for a5/geohash (token), icon (lat/lng/icon), or 3D (lat/lng/altitude or geojson).

options.description: Initial visual settings; inspect map.get-layer-options to discover editable keys.

variable.description: Variable path from the Zarr dataset metadata.

layerName.description: Generate a unique name for the layer based on the context.

flowField.description: For layerType "flowField" only: how the vector field is encoded. The mode is inferred from the columns (u/v, speed/direction, otherwise altitude); the *Column fields name the columns when they differ from those defaults.

simpleColor.description: The color of the layer e.g. [255, 0, 0]. Only used for simple map visualization (no colorBy, colorType, colorMap).

countColumn.description: For layerType "flow" (and only flow): a numeric column whose value weights each flow (flow magnitude). Omit to render all flows at weight 1.

tools.name: map_update-layer-color
tools.description: Update the color palette of an existing layer.

customColors.description: An array of hex color values. Try to generate colors from user description like: van gogh starry night, water color etc.

tools.name: map_load-data
tools.description: Load a dataset from a URL into kepler.gl. The dataset is named after the URL filename, or after `datasetName` when provided. Does NOT create a layer — call map.add-layer to visualize. Do NOT create a duplicate dataset (e.g. via map.create-table) just to rename it; name it here with `datasetName` instead, or use the URL-filename dataset as-is. LOCAL FILES: a local file must be served over http(s) — the browser cannot fetch `file://` paths. To load a file you have on disk: (1) copy it into the demo app's served directory (e.g. `examples/demo-app/dist/`) and pass `/filename.csv`, or (2) serve it with a CORS-enabled local server (`npx serve --cors -l 8000` in the file's folder) and pass `http://localhost:8000/filename.csv`. EMBEDDED CONTENT: if you have the file content but cannot serve it (e.g. a remote browser context), pass it as a data URL — `data:text/csv;base64,<base64 content>` (encode with `base64 -i file.csv`). Works for small files (up to ~2MB). LARGE DATASETS: for files over a few MB, prefer Parquet (.parquet) over GeoJSON/CSV — it loads much faster and is less likely to time out. Convert GeoJSON to GeoParquet with geopandas (`gdf.to_parquet("data.parquet")`); kepler reads GeoParquet geometry (WKB) natively.

url.description: The URL to load data from. May be a full http(s) URL, a path served by the demo app (e.g. /data.geojson), or a data URL embedding small file content (data:text/csv;base64,...).

datasetName.description: Optional name for the loaded dataset. If omitted, the URL filename is used. Use this instead of creating a duplicate dataset to rename it.

tools.name: map_load-zarr
tools.description: Read Zarr metadata and import a raster dataset without downloading all its chunks. Call map.add-layer with layerType "zarr" and the returned datasetId to visualize it. The store must allow browser access (CORS). Returns variable paths and non-spatial dimensions.

url.description: HTTP(S) root URL of a Zarr store, accessible from the browser.

variable.description: Optional variable path within the store.

tools.name: map_load-tileset
tools.description: Import remote layer metadata without downloading the whole dataset. Then call map.add-layer using the returned datasetId and layerType. URLs must be accessible from the browser (CORS). Raster supports STAC items/collections and PMTiles; 3D tiles accepts a tileset JSON URL.

url.description: MVT template or PMTiles archive, raster STAC/PMTiles URL, WMS service, 3D tileset JSON, or image URL.

metadataUrl.description: Vector TileJSON metadata URL; inferred from url when omitted.

rasterTileServerUrls.description: TiTiler servers for STAC rasters; required unless the host configures them. PMTiles does not need a server.

bounds.description: Required for bitmap: [west, south, east, north].

tools.name: map_get-layer-options
tools.description: Inspect editable visual settings, current values, ranges and choices for a layer. Use map.set-layer-options to update them. Zarr variable/dimension/axis changes use its zarr parameter.

tools.name: map_set-layer-options
tools.description: Patch visual settings using keys from map.get-layer-options. Supports point glow/pulse/ripple, heatmap surfaces, flow-field density/trails/timing, and model settings. Event pulses also require an enabled time filter on pulseTimeField. Use zarr for validated variable, dimension, axis, frame and rescale changes.

variable.description: Variable path from the Zarr dataset metadata.

wmsLayer.description: For WMS: a service layer name returned by map.get-layer-options or map.load-tileset.

tools.name: map_camera-bookmarks
tools.description: List, save, remove, navigate to camera bookmarks, or show-control without resaving. Save upserts by id, preserving other bookmarks and their order. Omit camera to capture the current view; pass showControl true to display the map bookmark control. Go-to moves immediately; split views target the primary pane and respect viewport sync/zoom lock.

id.description: Required for save, remove, and go-to.

camera.description: For save: omit to capture the current camera.

showControl.description: For save or show-control: show/hide the bookmark control.

tools.name: map_camera-tour
tools.description: Get or replace the saved location-animation tour, seek to elapsedMs, play or pause. Each stop holds before travelling to the next; the last travel duration is unused. Play resumes the shared player even with the side panel closed; manual camera navigation pauses it. Seek pauses and moves immediately. Split views target the primary pane and respect viewport sync/zoom lock; globe cameras use globe constraints.

stops.description: Required for set: ordered stops; [] clears the tour. Snapshots are independent of bookmarks.

tools.name: map_set-zoom-fade
tools.description: Enable/disable zoom fades or replace their controllers. Each layer/annotation can belong to only one controller. Stops must satisfy 0 <= appear <= full <= fade <= gone <= 24. Preserves other interactions and each layer’s own opacity.

controllers.description: Replaces the controller list. Omit to only toggle; [] clears it.

tools.name: map_save-data
tools.description: Save a DuckDB table to kepler.gl as a map dataset. Works with any table including those from buffer, zipcode, county, state, isochrone, routing, query results, etc.

datasetNames.description: The names of the DuckDB tables to load into kepler.gl.

tools.name: map_create-table
tools.description:
Create a NEW dataset in kepler.gl from a SQL query. The result becomes a SEPARATE new dataset (resultDatasetName); the ORIGINAL dataset and its layers/filters are left untouched. Use it to build a new table with different columns — e.g. add, delete, or rename columns, or change a column's type (CAST(col AS <type>)) — inside the new dataset.
NOTE: To modify an EXISTING dataset in place, do NOT use this command — use map.add-column instead (add a column that copies an existing one to "rename", or casts it via expression to change its type). Only reach for map.create-table when the user wants a NEW, separate dataset.
Please note:
1. Do not use * to select all columns, instead use all the column names in dataset.
2. List all column names the new table or dataset will have.
IMPORTANT: Use __TABLE__ as the table name placeholder in SQL. It will be replaced with the actual DuckDB table name at runtime.

datasetName.description: The name of the source dataset

variableNames.description: Only use variable names that already exist in the dataset.

sql.description: The SQL query to execute. Use __TABLE__ as the table name placeholder.

resultDatasetName.description: The name for the new dataset

tools.name: map_add-column
tools.description:
Add a NEW column to an existing kepler.gl dataset (table), in place. The dataset keeps its name, id, color and layers; existing columns are untouched, so layers, filters and tooltips keep working unchanged.
The new column's values come from exactly ONE of two sources:
- copyFromColumn — copy the values of an existing column. This is how you "rename" a column in place: to rename "fare" to "fare_amount", add a new column "fare_amount" that copies "fare" (the original "fare" column stays — this command never removes columns).
- expression — an SQL expression computed in DuckDB against the dataset's rows, e.g. a z-score: "(HR60 - AVG(HR60) OVER()) / STDDEV(HR60) OVER()" adds HR60_Z holding the standardized value of HR60. The expression may reference existing columns and window functions; it must produce exactly one value per row.
CHANGING A COLUMN'S TYPE: use expression to add a NEW column that casts the original, e.g. to turn "NOSOUTH" (numeric) into a string, add a new column with expression "NOSOUTH::VARCHAR" (or "CAST(NOSOUTH AS VARCHAR)"). The values become strings; the original column stays. Name the new column clearly (e.g. "NOSOUTH_str") or as the user requests.
IMPORTANT: this command only ADDS columns. It cannot delete or rename-in-place an existing column, and it never changes the type OF an existing column in place — a type change is achieved by adding a NEW column holding the cast values. If you need to remove columns or rebuild the whole table, use map.create-table (which creates a NEW dataset; the original is untouched).

datasetName.description: The name (label) or id of the dataset to add the column to

newColumnName.description: The name of the new column to add. Must not already exist in the dataset.

copyFromColumn.description: The name of an EXISTING column whose values the new column will copy. Mutually exclusive with `expression` — provide exactly one.

expression.description: An SQL expression computed in DuckDB against the dataset rows; the result becomes the new column. e.g. z-score: "(HR60 - AVG(HR60) OVER()) / STDDEV(HR60) OVER()". Mutually exclusive with `copyFromColumn` — provide exactly one.

tools.name: map_add-time-filter
tools.description:
Add a time-range filter to animate a NON-trip layer over a TIMESTAMP/DATE column. The time controller appears at the bottom of the map.

DO NOT call this for a trip layer — trips have built-in time animation.

The dataset and a layer for it must already exist on the map (e.g. from map.add-layer or map.load-data).

Pass the datasetName and the dateTimeColumn to animate over. The interval is auto-detected from the data when omitted; pass it explicitly to override.

datasetName.description: The name (label) or id of the dataset to animate.

dateTimeColumn.description: A TIMESTAMP or DATE column in the dataset. Do NOT pass an integer/string epoch column — build a real TIMESTAMP column first.

interval.description: Animation step. Auto-detected from the data span and distinct timestamps when omitted.

tools.name: map_toggle-time-filter
tools.description:
Show or hide the enlarged time controller at the bottom of the map.

A time filter must already exist on the map (created via map.add-time-filter).

- action: "show" — enlarge the time controller so it is visible at the bottom of the map.
- action: "hide" — collapse the time controller back to the side panel.

action.description: "show" enlarges the time controller at the bottom of the map; "hide" collapses it to the side panel.

filterIndex.description: Index of the time filter to toggle. If omitted, the first time-range filter found is used.

tools.name: map_split-view
tools.description:
Enable or disable the dual-map (split view) comparison mode.

When enabled, the map splits into two panels for side-by-side comparison. Pass layerIdsForMap0 / layerIdsForMap1 to assign which layers show ONLY in the left / right panel; without these, all layers show on both panels (no comparison).

When disabled, the map returns to a single panel.

Use the SAME colorBy / colorType for the layers being compared, so the comparison is fair.

action.description: "enable" activates dual map mode; "disable" returns to a single map.

layerIdsForMap0.description: Layer IDs to show ONLY in the LEFT panel. Layers not listed are hidden from the left panel.

layerIdsForMap1.description: Layer IDs to show ONLY in the RIGHT panel. Layers not listed are hidden from the right panel.

tools.name: map_get-dataset-context
tools.description: Get all loaded kepler.gl datasets with their fields and layer configurations. Returns each dataset name, id, field name→type mappings, and the layers (id, label, type, geometryMode, geometryColumns) bound to it.
